notes: CORRECTED 2026-10-03: AUDIT 2026-10-03 (flag semantics + NVL-column basis, no value changed): NVIDIA's H100 datasheet page-2 table carries a THREE-column header (H100 SXM / H100 PCIe / H100 NVL) and footnote 1 reads 'Specifications shown for 2x H100 NVL PCIe cards paired with NVLink Bridge'. The datasheet's NVL column therefore prints PAIRED aggregates - 188GB, 7.8TB/s, TF32 1,979, BF16/FP16 3,958, FP8/INT8 7,916 - whereas NVIDIA's own H100 product page 'Product Specifications' table prints a PER-CARD H100 NVL column: 94GB, 3.9TB/s, TF32 835, BF16/FP16 1,671, FP8/INT8 3,341, footnote '\* With sparsity'. This record's stored per-card values (94 GB / 3,938 GB/s / 417.5 TF32 / 835.5 BF16 / 1,670.5 FP8, all dense) are the correct PER-CARD figures and reconcile against the product page. Both readings are kept here because NVIDIA genuinely publishes two different NVL numbers for the same card and the difference is a card-vs-pair basis, not a contradiction. A reader who takes 188GB or 7.8TB/s as a per-accelerator figure will double the card's capacity and bandwidth. Sources acc2-nv-h100-datasheet-2023 (datasheet, 2x-pair basis) and nv-h100-product-page (per-card basis) prove both. AUDIT CORRECTION: the dense/sparse flag on the tensor rows was inverted. FP16 835.5 / FP8 1670.5 TFLOPS are DENSE; NVIDIA prints 1,671/3,341 'With sparsity'. These rows were previously flagged dense:false, which wrongly told a reader they were sparse.  The stored numbers are correct dense values. CRITICAL: datasheet prints 835 TF32 / 1,671 BF16+FP16 / 3,341 FP8+INT8 for H100 NVL, all WITH SPARITY; dense is half. Memory spec is fully primary-sourced (nv-h100-nvl-product-brief Table 2). CONFLICT on vram: the current NVIDIA product page (nv-h100-datasheet) says H100 NVL has 94GB, but the H100 NVL column there is a PER-CARD figure while the datasheet's own H100 NVL column is a 2x-paired aggregate (188GB, 7.8TB/s) - the datasheet footnote says specs for H100 NVL are 'shown for 2x H100 NVL PCIe cards paired with NVLink Bridge'. 94GB per card is the correct per-accelerator number and is what this record uses. tdp_w 400 is the >400W default from the product brief; the product page says 350-400W configurable. Notably this 94GB card has MORE bandwidth (3,938 GB/s) than the 80GB HBM3 SXM (3,350) while computing LESS. The 'other' row is FP64 30 TFLOPS (dense) - this schema's precision enum has no fp64 member.
